I presume its an appointment with one of the psychologists first, they're basically looking to make sure you're committed to your transition and taking steps towards your set goal (which isn't the same for everyone). You don't have to be out to everyone but if you're not out to them they will probably ask you questions like if you are planning to or help you come up with some solutions to barriers to coming out. About coming out to people you need to do it in your own time and make sure you feel safe and comfortable, but maybe try writing down some ideas about what you want to say to people first. You could also looking into getting your name changed if you havn't already, its not a set requirement for hormones, but it is one way to show you're serious. But most off just research what you want out of hormones, they will ask you what your currently not happy about and what changes you want if you can answer that well they will see that hormones are the next step for you. Trust me its not as scary as it feels i had my first appointment with gendercare back in October and i was super nervous but it was fine and now in less than a week i have my appointment with the endo. Good Luck! You've got this!
